mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased consistently over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month indicates supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a single month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which is bullish for the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in a single month and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 0.2% monthly increase), it indicates strong demand without significant inflationary pressure, which is positive for the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% in 1 month and CPIAUCSL increases < 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% and CPIAUCSL increased by less than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, which is generally positive for the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS decreased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% in a single month and real GDP (GDPC1) shows growth, it indicates a strong supply-side response to demand, which is positive for the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% in 1 month and GDPC1 shows growth
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% and GDPC1 showed growth.
